features.name: The active nucleus
features.facts: M51 has a Seyfert 2 active galactic nucleus: a supermassive black hole swallowing gas. A jet from it is disturbing the molecular gas within a few hundred light-years of the centre (Matsushita, Muller & Lim 2007, A&A 468, L49). Its mass is not given in the sources used here.

features.name: M51-ULS-1
features.facts: A high-mass X-ray binary found by the Chandra X-ray Observatory: a blue supergiant of about 20 solar masses and a compact companion (a neutron star or black hole of 1.4–10 solar masses), closer than 3 AU, 4–16 million years old. Gas pulled off the giant falls onto the companion and glows in X-rays. In 2020 a dip in its X-rays was reported as a possible planet, M51-ULS-1b, about the size of Saturn, orbiting both at ~45 AU every ~70 years — unconfirmed; if real, the first planet found in another galaxy.

observed.name: SN 1994I
observed.what: Core collapse of a star stripped of both its hydrogen and helium envelopes.

observed.name: SN 2005cs
observed.what: Core collapse of a red supergiant of about 7–13 solar masses; its progenitor star was found in earlier Hubble images.

observed.name: SN 2011dh
observed.what: Core collapse of a yellow supergiant that had lost most of its hydrogen envelope; a candidate progenitor was found in Hubble images.

observed.name: AT 2019abn
observed.what: Not a supernova: a "supernova impostor", later identified as a luminous red nova, probably two stars merging.
